figures.finding: Curaçao has no exemption for child performers: it is forbidden to let a child under fifteen do any work, paid or not, under contract or not; a national decree may exclude, from twelve, light work outside school hours and between 07:00 and 19:00; young persons of fifteen to eighteen may not work before 07:00 or after 19:00, nor do dangerous work.

figures.finding: Curaçao's age of majority is eighteen under article 233 of its Civil Code; majority also comes by marriage, or for an unmarried mother by a declaration of majority at sixteen, and a minor may perform legal acts with the legal representative's permission, presumed where minors of that age normally act alone (art. 234).
figures.applies: Curaçao (the Kingdom's 2014 report, Part four: Curaçao).

sources.said: Article 233 of the Civil Code sets the age of majority at 18 years
Majority is attained when a child reaches 18 years; upon marriage; or, in the case of unmarried mothers, through a declaration of majority when they reach the age of 16.
